skill_title: Define work, energy and power; calculate power
notes: 20 items: 10 lifted, 10 fresh. Definitions of work, conservative/non-conservative force, mechanical energy, power; calculations of P = W/t and P = Fv; basic KE and PE formulas.

items.question: Define POWER in words.
items.expectedAnswer: Power is the rate at which work is done, or equivalently the rate at which energy is transferred.
items.explanation: Two marks: 'rate' + 'work done / energy transferred'. P = W/t. SI unit watts (W = J/s).

items.question: Define a CONSERVATIVE force.
items.expectedAnswer: A force for which the work done in moving an object between two points is independent of the path taken (depends only on initial and final positions).
items.explanation: Examples: gravity, spring force, electrostatic force. The work depends only on start/end positions.

items.question: Define a NON-CONSERVATIVE force.
items.expectedAnswer: A force for which the work done in moving an object between two points DEPENDS on the path taken; the work done is not recoverable as mechanical energy.
items.explanation: Examples: friction, air resistance, applied force, normal during inelastic collisions. Work done varies with path; mechanical energy is not conserved when these forces act.

items.question: A demolition ball swings into a wall, causing the wall to crack and pieces of brick to fly off. Is the force the wall exerts on the ball CONSERVATIVE or NON-CONSERVATIVE? Give a reason.
items.expectedAnswer: Non-conservative. The work depends on the deformation/path; energy is dissipated as heat, sound and broken brick rather than being recoverable as mechanical energy.
items.explanation: Permanent deformation = energy lost. Non-conservative forces convert mechanical energy to other forms.

items.question: An object is moved along two different paths between the same two points. The same amount of work is done along both paths. Which TYPE of force is responsible?
items.explanation: By definition, a conservative force does the same amount of work between two points, regardless of path.

items.question: Describe the energy conversion that takes place as a demolition ball swings DOWNWARD from its highest point on a chain.
items.expectedAnswer: Gravitational potential energy is converted to kinetic energy.
items.explanation: As height decreases, PE decreases; speed increases, so KE increases. The chain (idealised as massless and inextensible) does no work, so mechanical energy is conserved.

items.question: A 1250 kg demolition ball is lifted to a height of 5.8 m in 60 s. Calculate the AVERAGE POWER used to lift the ball. (g = 9.8 m·s⁻².)
Engine P has a GREATER maximum power output than engine Q. Both engines operate at their maximum power for the SAME time interval. Which statement is CORRECT?
options: Engine P does LESS work than engine Q
Engines P and Q do equal work
Engine P does the SAME work as Q because time is the same
Engine P does MORE work than engine Q
items.expectedAnswer: Engine P does MORE work than engine Q
items.explanation: W = P × t. Same time, larger P ⇒ more work.

items.question: A 60 kg skier is towed back up a slope by a motor in 40 s. The vertical height gained is 80 m. Calculate the average power output of the tow lift. (g = 10 m·s⁻²; ignore friction during the tow.)
An object moving with velocity v has kinetic energy E. If its velocity DOUBLES, its kinetic energy becomes:
items.explanation: KE = ½mv². Doubling v multiplies v² (and KE) by 4.

items.question: Define the WORK done by a constant force on an object as it undergoes a displacement.
items.expectedAnswer: Work done = F·d·cosθ, where F is the magnitude of the force, d is the displacement, and θ is the angle between the force and the displacement.
items.explanation: Two marks: 'F·d·cosθ' OR explicit statement including the angle between F and d. Forgetting cosθ is a common slip.

items.question: A 60 N horizontal force pulls a box 5 m across a horizontal floor. Calculate the work done by the applied force.
items.explanation: Force and displacement are parallel (θ = 0°, cosθ = 1). W = Fd = 60 × 5 = 300 J.

items.question: A 200 N force is applied at 30° above the horizontal to a box that moves 8 m horizontally. Calculate the work done by the applied force.

A waiter carries a 2 kg tray horizontally across a room at constant height. The tray is held at 1 m above the floor for the whole journey. How much work is done by the waiter on the tray AGAINST GRAVITY?
items.explanation: Tray moves horizontally; gravity acts vertically. θ = 90°, cosθ = 0 ⇒ no work done against gravity. The waiter exerts an upward force but does no work because there is no vertical displacement.

items.question: Which of the following is a NON-conservative force?
items.explanation: Friction work depends on path length (longer path ⇒ more energy dissipated). Gravity, spring, and electrostatic forces are conservative.

items.question: A 1500 kg car drives up a hill with a constant velocity of 15 m·s⁻¹. The engine produces a constant driving force of 4000 N. Calculate the instantaneous power developed by the engine.
items.explanation: P = Fv = 4000 × 15 = 60 000 W (= 60 kW). At constant velocity, instantaneous power equals applied force times velocity.

items.question: What is the SI unit of POWER?
items.explanation: 1 W = 1 J/s. Power = energy per unit time, so units must be J/s.

items.question: A pump lifts 200 kg of water through a vertical height of 8 m in 25 seconds. Calculate the average power developed by the pump. (g = 9.8 m·s⁻².)
A 50 N box is pushed 10 m across a rough surface by a 50 N applied force. Friction is 30 N. Calculate the net work done on the box.
Define MECHANICAL ENERGY of an object.
items.expectedAnswer: The sum of the gravitational potential energy and the kinetic energy of the object: E_mech = PE + KE = mgh + ½mv².
items.explanation: Mechanical energy includes only kinetic and gravitational potential energy in CAPS context. Heat, sound and chemical energy are not part of mechanical energy.

_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_POWER_DEF: Power definition missing 'rate' or 'work / energy transfer'
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_CONSERVATIVE_DEF: Definition of conservative/non-conservative force missing path-dependence language
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_CONSERVATIVE_IDENTIFY: Misidentifies a force as conservative or non-conservative
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_ENERGY_CONVERSION_DIRECTION: Reverses direction of energy conversion (PE → KE on descent)
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_POWER_FORMULA: Misapplies P = W/t (e.g. multiplies instead of divides)
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_GPE_FORMULA: Uses wrong formula for gravitational PE
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_KE_SQUARED_VELOCITY: Treats KE as linear in v instead of v²
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_WORK_DEF_OMITS_COSINE: Defines work without the cosθ between F and d
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_TRIG_RESOLUTION: Wrong trig ratio in component decomposition
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_WORK_NO_DISPLACEMENT: Computes nonzero work when displacement is perpendicular to force
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_POWER_FV: Doesn't recognise P = Fv as instantaneous power at constant velocity
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_POWER_UNIT: Names the wrong SI unit for power
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_NET_WORK_SUM_SIGN: Sign error when summing positive and negative work contributions
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_MECH_ENERGY_DEF: Mechanical energy definition omits PE or KE
